::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 5th 1888  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge IV 6
:::

Dear [Mr Innes](people/person_744.qmd)

The copies to [Canon Warburton](people/person_1466.qmd) were for presentation to the Central libraries of our [Diocesan Society for Higher Religious Education](organizations/other_48.qmd).[^1]

I imagine that half a sheet will be quite enough, giving me 4 pages besides those for index and title which I always grudge but I cannot tell till I get the list of make up.

I see Chapman and Hall’s M S will not do. I much dislike stories in dialect and indeed I think everyone does except the author, and philologists.  What shall I do with it?

I like [Pen](other_books/otherbook_1072.qmd) much better than [Tipcat](other_books/otherbook_1070.qmd) or [Our Little Ann](other_books/otherbook_1071.qmd).[^2]

My own feeling is that we can hardly be accountable for <u>respectable</u> advertisements I see [A South African farm](other_books/otherbook_1069.qmd) among them and I believe that is far worse than [Robert Elsmere](other_books/otherbook_631.qmd)[^3]

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The copies were probably of CMY's *Preparation of Prayer-book Lessons*.
[^2]: These were stories by a Smith and Innes author, [Evelyn Whitaker](people/person_1492.qmd).  In 'A Conversation on Books' (*MP* (December 1888), 590, CMY praised *Pen* and observed, 'Her style is always charming, but there were too great improbabilities in Tip Cat and Little Ann.'
[^3]: A reader had complained that her copy of *MP* had arrived with advertisements for a novel by Mary Augusta Ward, author of the controversial novel *Robert Elsmere*.
